sections.h2: Where is Dodge County, Georgia, and which towns does it hold?
sections.html:
Dodge County lies in the southern part of Georgia, mostly in the Ocmulgee River watershed, and Eastman is both the seat of government and the biggest city. Wikipedia gives a total area of 503 square miles, of which the Census Bureau counts 495.96 as land.

The legislature organized the county on October 26, 1870, carving it mostly from Laurens County with smaller pieces of Pulaski, Montgomery and Telfair. The Macon and Brunswick Railroad had been built the year before, and towns grew up along the line far from the old county seat at Hawkinsville. Chauncey, Eastman and Milan are cities. Chester and Rhine are towns, and Empire is a census-designated place that crosses into Bleckley County.

Highways include US 23, US 280, US 341 and the US 319 and 441 corridor, plus State Routes 46 and 117 and several others. The Heart of Georgia Regional Airport lies three miles east of Eastman on State Route 46 and houses an aviation campus of Middle Georgia State College. A seller in Dodge County is usually dealing with a rural or small-town parcel, and the county's own offices handle nearly every step.

sections.h2: Who do Dodge County owners call about property tax?
sections.html:
On the county's services page, the Tax Commissioner is 478-374-2154 and the Tax Assessors are 478-374-8122. County government works out of 643 Pearl Bates Avenue in Eastman, and the clerk of courts answers at 478-374-2871.

State guidance divides the roles the same way statewide: the commissioner takes payments and, in most counties, homestead filings, while the assessors own the appraised value and appeal questions. The county website has a Tax Payments link for paying online. The cities and towns inside the county publish these numbers:

  • Chauncey: 229-868-2296
  • Chester: 478-358-4550
  • Eastman: 478-374-7721
  • Milan: 229-362-4290
  • Rhine: 229-385-5521

If your house sits inside a city, ask both the county and the city clerk whether city tax comes on a separate bill.

sections.h2: Has the 2026 assessment appeal window in Dodge County closed?
sections.html:
Dodge County mailed its 2026 tax assessment notices on June 19, 2026, and August 3, 2026 was the final day to appeal. For the 2026 digest that window is shut, so a seller who missed it lives with the 2026 value and watches for next year's notice.

The county announcement says appeals could be filed by email, by U.S. mail, or online through the appeal module on the qPublic site. Anyone who did not receive a notice, or who has a question about one, was told to call the assessors at 478-374-8122. The notice arrives every year, and the 45 days run from the day it was mailed, so mark the mailing date when it comes.

The county also raised the processing fee for conservation use (CUVA), forest land protection (FLPA) and other preferential parcels to $30.00 for new, renewal and continuation covenants, effective July 1, 2025. Owners of farm or timber land should ask the assessors whether a covenant is recorded on the parcel before listing.

sections.h2: What are my appeal options once I file in Dodge County?
sections.html:
The state's uniform appeal form makes you pick one of three tracks, and the completed form is sent to the Dodge County Board of Tax Assessors. State revenue staff have no power to override a local value.

TrackWhat it coversWhat happens next
Board of EqualizationValue, uniformity, taxability or a denied exemptionAssessors may revise the notice; if not, a hearing is scheduled and a decision follows
Hearing officerValue or uniformity of non-homestead real property worth more than $500,000Decision, then superior court if still disputed
ArbitrationValue onlyTaxpayer submits a certified appraisal within 45 days of the acknowledgment; hearing scheduled within 30 days

Table source: Georgia Department of Revenue, Filing a Property Tax Appeal.

  • Going to superior court takes a written notice to the assessors inside 30 days after the ruling
  • The board schedules a settlement conference after your appeal, with notice inside 45 days
  • The court will not hear the case until last year's amount of tax is paid
  • A final value at 85 percent or less of the earlier figure lets the taxpayer recover costs and attorney's fees

sections.h2: When are Dodge County property taxes due?
sections.html:
The state default is December 20, and a county may instead choose December 1, November 15 or installments. Interest also waits until 60 days after the bill was postmarked. Whatever date your Dodge bill prints controls, and the commissioner at 478-374-2154 can replace a lost bill.

Delinquent balances can pick up penalties on top of interest. Ask the tax commissioner what your parcel owes before a closing, request the figure in writing, and give a copy to whoever runs the closing.

A return of value can be filed from January 1 through April 1. An owner who paid last year and files nothing is treated as repeating last year's final value, so most homeowners never file one.

sections.h2: Does Dodge County offer homestead exemptions?
sections.html:
State revenue records show no local homestead exemptions in Dodge County beyond the statewide ones. An application can go in any time after the house becomes your primary residence, with April 1 as the cutoff for the first year of benefit.

Skipping the application forfeits that year's exemption. The standard state exemption takes $2,000 off assessed value, which is set at 40 percent of fair market value. The county's tax commissioner or assessors take the application, depending on how Dodge handles it, so ask which window applies.

Refunds exist for tax assessed or collected in error, with a claim due inside three years of payment. A seller does not get part of a year back, since ownership on January 1 fixes liability for the whole year.

sections.h2: What should a Dodge County seller know about taxes at closing?
sections.html:
The January 1 owner is liable for that year's bill, so a fall sale still carries a full year of tax. The sales contract decides how the year is split, and the closing statement shows who pays what.

Two recorded items matter at closing. A security deed on a long-term loan must be recorded in the county within 90 days, and the intangible tax on it is $1.50 for every $500 of the note, collected by the superior court clerk in most counties. A sale also triggers transfer tax, which the seller owes by law and which the Department of Revenue prints as $1 for the first $1,000 plus 10 cents for each added $100. A county tax lien is entered on the general execution docket at the clerk's office, which is where a title search finds it.

sections.h2: How big and how priced is the Dodge County housing stock?
sections.html:
QuickFacts lists 19,663 residents for 2025, a 1.7% drop since April 2020, along with 8,643 housing units and just 5 building permits for the year.

  • Share of homes lived in by their owners: 70.6%
  • Middle home value: $118,100
  • Median gross rent: $723
  • Median household income: $51,587
  • Residents 65 and older: 20.8%
  • People per square mile (2020): 40.2

For comparison, the same table gives $357,800 for DeKalb County, so a Dodge County house sits at a much lower price point. Check the parcel's tax status before you list, since a back-tax balance weighs more against a lower sale price.

faqs.q: Which number reaches Dodge County's tax office?
faqs.a: Call the Dodge County Tax Commissioner at 478-374-2154. The Tax Assessors, at 478-374-8122, answer questions about values and appeals.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal my 2026 Dodge County assessment?
faqs.a: For the 2026 digest, yes. Notices were mailed June 19, 2026, and August 3 was the final day was August 3, 2026. Watch for the next annual notice and count 45 days from its mailing date.

faqs.q: Does Dodge County have its own homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No. State records list none beyond the statewide exemption, which owners request through the county tax office by April 1 of the first benefit year.

faqs.q: When are Dodge County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The state default is December 20 unless the county sets another date or installments. Owners also get 60 days from the bill's postmark before interest. Use the date printed on your bill.

faqs.q: Can I get property tax back after selling my Dodge County house?
faqs.a: Georgia law does not refund a partial year, because the January 1 owner is liable for all of it. A refund is available only for tax assessed or collected in error, with a claim within three years of payment.
